label: Bible Study
prompt: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became _____, that ye through his poverty might be rich.
verse: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich.
note: The Christmas story as an exchange — he became poor so we could become rich.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how _____ things he hath done for you.
verse: Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you.
note: Samuel's farewell advice: serve the LORD in truth, and just consider the great things He has done for you.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And they said one to another, Behold, this _____ cometh.
verse: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.
note: Joseph's brothers spotted him coming across the field and sneered, 'Behold, this dreamer cometh' — the dreams came true anyway.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Through faith we understand that the worlds were _____ by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.
verse: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.
note: Creation from nothing visible — the Hall of Faith's very first exhibit is the universe itself.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and _____ the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
verse: And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
note: God's first words to humankind were a blessing with a commission attached: multiply, 'replenish' the earth, and subdue it.
